title: Anger Symbol Emoji 💢 Meaning: The Manga Vein Pop
description: 💢 is the manga sign for a throbbing vein, meaning anger or irritation. It is not a flower or an explosion. See how it is used and what people confuse it with.
summary: The 💢 anger symbol emoji means irritation or rage. It comes from Japanese manga and anime, where four curved red marks drawn on a character's forehead represent a bulging vein. In messages it shows annoyance, usually exaggerated and half-joking, and it is often added to an angry face.
meaning: Readers of manga recognize 💢 instantly. Artists draw it on a character's temple, forehead or clenched fist at the moment they lose patience, as a stylized picture of veins swelling under the skin. It is a piece of visual grammar in the same family as the giant sweat drop for embarrassment or the snot bubble for sleep. The emoji lifts that mark out of the comic panel so it can be used alone.

In texting it signals that the sender is ticked off. The mood is usually cartoon anger: outrage at a spoiler, a sibling who ate the leftovers, a game that crashed before saving. Because the symbol is so stylized, it softens the emotion and tells the reader this is venting, not a real threat. People who are seriously upset tend to use words or a plain 😡 instead.

Outside anime-literate circles, plenty of users have no idea what it depicts. It gets read as a red flower, a spark, a collision or a generic “impact” sign, and it is sometimes used that way, for emphasis or for things bumping together. That ambiguity is worth remembering when you send it to someone who does not watch anime, since the intended irritation may not register.

Fans, gamers and VTuber communities use it most. It decorates reaction images, stream chats and captions about a character's short temper, and it is a regular in posts about tsundere characters, the type who hide affection behind irritation. Japanese-language posts use it far more freely than English ones, often tacked to the end of a sentence like punctuation.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It works as a compact “I'm annoyed.” Typical triggers are small: a late bus, a friend who left you on read, a spoiler in the group chat. Putting 💢 after a complaint adds comic heat. Doubling or tripling it raises the level, but it remains playful compared with typing in capitals or sending an enraged face.

contexts.label: In anime and manga fandom
contexts.body: Fans use it exactly as artists do. It is attached to screenshots of irritated characters, used in role-play to show a character's temper flaring, and dropped into replies as a reaction. In these spaces everyone understands the reference, and it often conveys fond amusement at a hot-headed favorite.

contexts.label: In gaming
contexts.body: Stream chats and Discord servers fill with 💢 when a boss fight goes wrong, a teammate misplays or a gacha pull disappoints. It expresses salt without breaking chat rules on abuse. Some players also use it for hits and impacts, treating it as a strike effect, which overlaps with the collision emoji.

contexts.label: Around the world
contexts.body: In Japan the mark is everyday visual language, seen in advertising, stickers and children's comics, so the emoji needs no explanation there. Elsewhere its meaning depends on exposure to Japanese pop culture. Older or less online recipients in English-speaking countries are the most likely to mistake it for a decorative red shape.

confusedWith.difference: 💥 is a starburst for crashes, explosions and impact. 💢 is specifically the anger vein. They look loosely similar as red-orange bursts, and some people swap them, but only the collision emoji actually means “boom.”
🗯️ is a jagged speech bubble for shouted or furious words. 💢 marks the feeling on a character's body. In comics the bubble holds the yelling, while the vein shows the temper that caused it.
😡 is a red, scowling face that anyone can read as anger, and it can come across as serious. 💢 is more abstract and more playful, and it relies on the recipient knowing the manga convention.

avoid: Do not use it to express serious anger at someone; it reads as cartoonish and may undercut your point.
Avoid assuming everyone knows it; with people unfamiliar with anime it may look like a flower or a random symbol.
Leave it out of professional complaints, where clear wording works better.
design: Four short, curved red strokes arranged around an empty center, like the corners of a puffy cross. This is the manga shorthand for veins standing out on an angry character's head. Vendors render it in bright red with minor differences in thickness and gloss, and the design has been stable since it was standardized in 2010 from the Japanese carrier sets.

faqs.q: What is the 💢 emoji supposed to be?
faqs.a: It is a stylized throbbing vein, sometimes called a cross-popping vein or anger mark. Manga and anime artists place it on a character's forehead to show irritation or fury. It is not a flower, a firework or a plus sign.

faqs.q: Does 💢 mean someone is really angry at me?
faqs.a: Usually not in a serious way. The symbol is theatrical, and people mostly use it for mild or joking annoyance. If the accompanying words are sharp, take those seriously; the emoji alone is rarely a sign of real hostility.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 💢 and 💥?
faqs.a: The anger symbol is an emotion marker for irritation. The collision emoji is an impact or explosion. In comics, 💢 sits on a person's head, while 💥 appears where two things crash together.

faqs.q: Why is 💢 used so much in anime communities?
faqs.a: Because it is taken directly from the art style those fans know. It lets them express a character-like burst of temper in text, and it is tied to familiar character types such as the hot-headed rival or the tsundere.

faqs.q: Can 💢 mean anything other than anger?
faqs.a: Some people use it loosely for emphasis, impact or pain, such as a pulsing headache, and a few treat it as decoration without knowing the origin. Those uses are secondary. Its defined meaning is anger.
